tool.name: annotateMyIDs
tool.description: Annotate a list of IDs using Bioconductor annotation data packages.
tool.command: Rscript --vanilla -e 'library(BiocManager); BiocManager::install("org.Hs.eg.db"); library(org.Hs.eg.db); library(AnnotationDbi); args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly=FALSE); input_file <- sapply(strsplit(args[grep("--input", args)], "="), "[[", 2); output_file <- sapply(strsplit(args[grep("--output", args)], "="), "[[", 2); id_type <- sapply(strsplit(args[grep("--id_type", args)], "="), "[[", 2); columns <- sapply(strsplit(args[grep("--columns", args)], "="), "[[", 2); df <- read.table(input_file, header=TRUE, sep="\t", stringsAsFactors=FALSE); res <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, keys=df[[1]], column=columns, keytype=id_type, multiVals="first"); write.table(res, file=output_file, sep="\t", quote=FALSE, col.names=NA)

param.name: input_file
param.label: Input File
param.help: Tab-delimited file with identifiers in the first column.

param.name: id_type
param.label: ID Type
param.help: Type of identifiers in the input file.

param.name: columns
param.label: Columns to Retrieve
param.help: Comma-separated list of columns to add to the output. Available columns depend on the input ID type.

tool.help:
This tool annotates a list of IDs using Bioconductor annotation data packages. Supported organisms are human, mouse, rat, fruit fly, and zebrafish. The org.db packages used here are primarily based on mapping using Entrez Gene identifiers.
Examples of what this tool can be used for include:
* Adding gene names to IDs * Mapping between IDs (e.g., Entrez, Ensembl, Symbols) * Adding GO and KEGG identifiers
This tool uses the `select` function from the Bioconductor AnnotationDbi package. Note that if you request columns that have multiple matches for your IDs, `select` will return one row in the output for each possible match. This can lead to multiplication of results if requesting multiple columns with many-to-one relationships.
